usage: Run from the journey worktree (C:/kipindi-journey, Playwright 1.59.1), detached under ~/heavy-node-lock.sh, alone, never piped. It needs a fresh in-memory dev server that no other drive is using: rm -rf .next, then DISABLE_ADMIN_TOTP=true npx next dev -p 3041, with no DATABASE_URL. Then run: KP_BASE=http://localhost:3041 npm run qa:journey-shell -- <outDir> (or node scripts/qa-journey-shell.mjs <outDir>). The outDir must be outside the repository; an outDir inside it is refused with exit 2. Leave it out and the tiles go to a new folder under the OS temp directory; the last line names it. KP_ONLY takes a comma list of these sections: classic, header, sheet, unread, wallet, focus, tabs, tickets, hub, overlays, viewer, emailbar, kyc. The sections always run in that order, and an unknown name is refused. On Git Bash, write KP_ONLY without leading slashes. KP_BUDGET_MIN (default 20) caps the cells after section 0. Once it is spent, each remaining section and page prints a BLOCKED line by name. KP_WARM_MIN (default 10) caps the warm-up. A watchdog ends the run at KP_WARM_MIN + KP_BUDGET_MIN + 5 minutes. Exit codes: 0 means every line passed; 1 means at least one FAIL; 2 means REFUSED; 3 means no FAIL but something BLOCKED. REFUSED covers: not http://localhost:PORT, a configured database, a withdrawn rollout, a bad KP_ONLY or minutes value, an outDir inside the repo, or the server changing during the run. Under the ACTIVE rollout the classic section and the email-bar control are BLOCKED; they need STAFF_PREVIEW. Expect about 335 viewport tiles over about 115 page loads. That is roughly 12 minutes of cells, plus a warm-up of 5 to 8 minutes just after rm -rf .next. Tiles are named NNN--section--route--viewer--state--locale--width.png. Read them in number order.

Review fixes, part 4 (safety). Budget and breaker: KP_BUDGET_MIN (default 20) is counted after section 0, and KP_WARM_MIN (default 10) bounds the warm-up. visit() and section() print BLOCKED by name once the budget is spent. Three unanswered loads or requests in a row block everything left. A watchdog fires at warm + budget + 5 minutes and exits 3, or 1 if anything FAILed. TOCTOU: guard() runs before every server-changing request: each dev-test POST, each demo session, seededSession, the pass mint, the displacement and B's form submit. It re-runs premise() and requires /api/health uptimeSec to be at least the start uptime plus elapsed time minus 30 s; otherwise it prints REFUSED and exits 2 before the request is sent. Dev overlay: after hydration, visit() adds the repo's own style tag hiding nextjs-portal (CSP style-src allows unsafe-inline). It FAILs a load when a Next error dialog is present (also checked inside the portal's shadow root) or the body shows an error page's words. outDir: resolved, and refused (exit 2) when it falls inside the repo root computed from import.meta.url. Dev-test routes are warmed by GET (each answers 405 and runs nothing) with a 300 s timeout, so mintStaffPass and seed-wallet do not hit Playwright's 30 s default on a cold server. warm() now runs in section 0 with a throwaway demo session, so protected pages compile instead of redirecting. Speed: one context per viewer is navigated route to route, so chunks are cached per viewer. The channels panel is suppressed outside section 10 (CHANNELS_DONE), so its 45 s dwell cannot land on an arbitrary tile.

Rule compliance and known limits. The file contains no backslash and no double-quote character. Newlines inside strings come from String.fromCharCode(10), the HTML quote is String.fromCharCode(34), regexes use only character classes, and CSS attribute values are single-quoted inside template literals. Every backticked script name in its comments exists in package.json once qa:journey-shell is added (guards-exist). Known limits: (1) the presence lines on /help and /account assume the AI toolkit's chatbot is ON (the in-memory default); (2) catalogue questions have no zh title, so a zh settled card can read English; (3) the new #main-content sweeps at 320 may surface real overflow that landmark-seal never measured (it runs 360 and up); read those as findings; (4) an Up & Down round settling during a /updown tile can draw the result announcer; the dialog-cover check will name it; (5) invite, proposals and agent hub doors follow the server's own state and are BLOCKED by name when absent; (6) G1 assumes B's inbox is empty (a fresh seed-admin account) and prints B's own count if it is not.

Not run. Under the hard rules I ran no node, npm, npx or Playwright, so the drive has never executed. On its first run, read each FAIL and BLOCKED line for a selector or timing a real render disagrees with before trusting the totals. Three are most likely: the hub walk's step count, the bell's remount time after the 390-to-1280 resize, and the login form typing. The cell count (about 335) and the time (about 12 minutes of cells plus the warm-up) are estimates.
